s: Which of the following disease may be caused due to deficiency of Vitamin C?
src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
x: Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy (bleeding gums, poor wound healing).

s: Which of the following is a major source of Vitamin C?
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: Gooseberry (amla) is the richest common source of vitamin C.

s:
Which of the following statement is/are not true about vitamins?

a. The term vitamin was coined by C Funk

b. Vitamins are organic compounds.

c. Vitamin K plays important role in clotting of blood.

d. Vitamin A, D, E and K are water soluble vitamins.
src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
x: Statements a (Funk coined 'vitamine'), b (vitamins are organic) and c (K for clotting) are true; d is false because A, D, E and K are fat-soluble. So only d.

s: The smallest ketone has ____ carbon atom/s.
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
x: The smallest ketone is acetone (propanone, CH3COCH3) with 3 carbon atoms, since the C=O must be bonded to two carbons. (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

s:
Match the following items with the acids found in them.
Natural source:

I. Orange

II. Tamarind

III. Tomato
Acid:

a. Tartaric Acid

b. Oxalic Acid

c. Citric Acid
src: APPSC Town Planning Building Overseers General Studies & Men
x: Orange - citric (c), tamarind - tartaric (a), tomato - oxalic (b): I-c, II-a, III-b (options 2 and 4 are printed identically).

List-II (Source):

x: Citric - lemon, oxalic - tomato, lactic - curd, acetic - vinegar: a-2, b-1, c-4, d-3.

s: Which of the following is pseudocereal
src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
x: Buckwheat (kuttu) is a pseudocereal: its seeds are used like grain but it is not a grass (family Polygonaceae). Amaranth and quinoa are other pseudocereals.

s: Which of the following is known as wheat protein?
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
x: Gluten is the protein of wheat that gives dough its elasticity.

s:
Arrange the following food items in the increasing order of the protein content per 100 gm of food.

a. Egg white
b. Bengalgram dal
c. Fish
d. Skimmed milk powder
e. Groundnuts
Select the appropriate option
at: a, c, b, e and d
src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
x: Protein per 100 g rises from egg white (~11 g) to fish (~20 g), Bengal gram dal (~21 g), groundnut (~25 g) and skimmed milk powder (~35 g). So a, c, b, e, d.

s: Which one of the following is not considered as a macronutrient?
src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
x: Macronutrients are needed in large amounts and give energy or bulk: carbohydrates, proteins and fats. Minerals (and vitamins) are needed in small amounts and are classed as micronutrients.

s:
Which of the following are symptoms of food allergy?

a. Nervousness

b. Fall in blood pressure

c. Atherosclerosis

d. Flushing of the skin

e. Difficulty in swallowing and speaking
src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
x: Food allergy can cause a fall in blood pressure (anaphylaxis), flushing or hives, and swelling of the throat with difficulty in swallowing and speaking. Atherosclerosis is a chronic artery disease, and nervousness is not a typical allergic sign.

s: No. of lobes present in left lung of cow
src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
x:
Most keys: 3 lobes (apical/cranial, cardiac/middle, diaphragmatic/caudal). Strictly in current veterinary nomenclature the left lung has 2 lobes, the cranial lobe being split into two parts (general knowledge, not checked).
Classical veterinary anatomy divides the ox's left lung into three lobes (apical, cardiac, diaphragmatic); the right lung has four or five.

s:
Read the following statements in respect to difference between 'Poisonous and Venomous animals':

a. If you bite it and you die, it's Poisonous. If it bites and you die, it's Venomous.

b. If you bite it and you die, it's Venomous. If it bites and you die, it's Poisonous.
Which of the above statements is/ are correct?
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: Poisonous animals harm you when you bite or eat them (toxin passively delivered); venomous animals inject venom by biting or stinging. So only statement a is correct.

s: Which of the following waves are used for common TV remote control?
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: Common TV remote controls use infrared (IR) light-emitting diodes. Off-topic (physics), moved.

s:
Which of the following is/are correct about Galvanometer?

1. It is a device used to detect electric current in a circuit.

2. It shows the direction of current flows in the circuit.

3. The accuracy of the galvanometer is more as compared to the ammeter.

4. The Galvanometer is mostly used in bridge for knowing the zero current.
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: A galvanometer detects current and its direction and serves as the null detector in bridges (1, 2, 4); it is more sensitive but not more accurate than an ammeter (3 wrong). Off-topic (physics), moved.

s:
Consider the following statements in respect of 'pi' (π)

a. Pi is the ratio of the circumference of a circle to its diameter.

b. Pi is a rational number
Which of the above statement/s is/are correct?
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
x: Only a is correct: pi is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter, and it is irrational (Aryabhata's 3.1416 is only an approximation), so statement b is false.

s: An ISSN is a ____ digits code for publications.
src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
x: An ISSN (International Standard Serial Number) has 8 digits, written as two groups of four.

s: A machined readable code consisting of vertical bars of varying widths to represent data is known as
src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
x: A barcode is a machine-readable code of vertical bars of varying widths (APPSC 2019).

s: Which of the following best describes a private, company wide network, closed to public access?
src: Miscellaneous Exams
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Intranet); it is added as option 6.
A private, company-wide network closed to public access is an intranet. The printed options repeat 'Internet' (option b is evidently a misprint of 'Intranet'); a VPN is a secure tunnel over a public network, cloud computing is remote services, and an extranet opens part of the network to outsiders.

s:
Consider the following statements with respect to "QR Code"

a. QR is short for Quick Response and can be read quickly by a cell phone.

b. QR code is the trademark for a type of matrix barcode first designed in 1996 for the automotive industry in Japan.
Select the correct code
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
x: QR = Quick Response, a matrix barcode read quickly by a phone camera, so a is right. b is wrong on the date: Denso Wave designed it in 1994, not 1996, for Japan's car industry.

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: E-mail delivers messages instantly and carries attachments (a-IV). A listserv is a mailing list linking people with shared interests (b-III). Video conferencing combines video, audio and data between places (c-II). Instant messaging is real-time text exchange (d-I).

s: In which of the following activities silicon carbide is used?
src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
x: Silicon carbide (carborundum) is extremely hard, so it is used as an abrasive for cutting and grinding very hard substances (it is also a power semiconductor).

s: As on March 2018, which of the following is the India's fastest supercomputer?
src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspectors, Agriculture Office
x: Pratyush (IITM Pune, unveiled January 2018, ~6.8 petaflops) was India's fastest supercomputer as of March 2018 (the question is dated; India's later AI system AIRAWAT ranked 75th in Top500 in 2023).

s: Optic fiber is mainly used for which of the following?
src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
x: Optical fibres carry signals by total internal reflection and are used mainly for communication (telecom, internet, cable TV).

s: What is SWAYAM?
o: Study Webs of Active-Learning for Young Aspiring Minds.
Study Webs of Active-Learning for Young Aspiration Minds.
Study Webs of Active-Learning for Young Aspiration Minds.
Study Webs of Active-Learning for Youth Aspiration Minds.
src: CDS 2019
x: SWAYAM stands for Study Webs of Active-Learning for Young Aspiring Minds; the other options alter 'Young Aspiring'.

s: Which of the following is a project floated under the National e-Governance Programme under mission mode?
src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
x: e-Panchayat is a State Mission Mode Project under NeGP.

s:
Consider the following statements.

a. 'MySecurity.in' is a web portal that will be a platform for innovation in the field of security related web applications.

b. It will be launched by Ministry of Home Affairs.

c. Any individual, company, student, NGO etc. can develop and deploy on this portal such security applications which may be useful to the public.
Which of the above statements are correct.
src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspectors, Agriculture Office
x: MySecurity.in was planned as an MHA web portal where any individual, company, student or NGO can develop and deploy security applications useful to the public, so all three statements are correct.

s:
Which of the following is/are correct?

a. ASTROSAT is India's first astronomical satellite.

b. GSAT-6 is the 25th geostationary communication satellite of India built by DRDO.

c. Kepler is a space observatory launched by ISRO.
src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
x: Only a: ASTROSAT (2015) is India's first dedicated astronomy satellite. GSAT-6 was built by ISRO, not DRDO, and Kepler was NASA's observatory.

s:

s: Which of the following is an application of Remote Sensing?
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
x: Remote sensing is used for land use, agriculture, forestry, water, disasters and more, so 'all of the given options'.

s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding Swayam Prabha?
at: It is a group of educational DTH television channels
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
x: Swayam Prabha is a group of 40 free educational DTH channels carried on GSAT-15.

s: Which of the following combinations can be used as both primary and final energy resources?
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: Coal, petroleum and natural gas are primary sources that can also be used directly as final energy (coal in industry and homes, gas as PNG/CNG, petroleum as fuel), so both pairs qualify.

s: Which of the following constitutes the maximum share in power generation in India?
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
x: Thermal power (mainly coal) gives the largest share of India's electricity generation, over 70%; coal is about 55% of the energy mix.

s: The mission of the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) is a.Energy Security b.Increase in share of clean power c.Energy availability and access d.Energy affordability e.Energy equity
o: Only a, c, d and e
src: APPSC Group-2 PYQ
x: MNRE's mission covers all five: energy security, a bigger share of clean power, availability and access, affordability and equity.

s: Which of the following takes the responsibility to even out supply-demand mismatches in the power supply in India?
src: APPSC Assistant B.C. Welfare Officer, Assistant Social Welfa
x: The integrated national (all-India) power grid moves power between regions and so evens out supply-demand mismatches.

s: Which of the following lamps is the cheapest for the same wattage?
src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
x: The General Lighting Service (incandescent) lamp has the lowest first cost for a given wattage, though it is the least efficient.

s: Which of the following is present inside the fluorescent tube?
src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
x: A fluorescent tube holds low-pressure mercury vapour (with argon); the mercury emits UV, which the phosphor turns into visible light.

s:
Consider the following statements-

a. An Ultra mega solar park is one which at a single location has total installed capacity of 1,000MW.

b. The Kurnool Ultra mega solar park in Andhra Pradesh is the world's largest single location solar park.
Which of the given statement's is/are correct?
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
x: An Ultra Mega Solar Park needs 500 MW or more, not 1,000 MW, so a is wrong. Kurnool (1,000 MW) was the world's largest single-location solar park, so b is right.

s: Which of the following is the most stable ecosystem?
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
x: The ocean (marine ecosystem) is the most stable ecosystem; it stays largely unchanged over long periods.

s: Which of the following is not a function of the tree?
src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
x: Trees reduce air pollution and give shade, oxygen and soil conservation; causing air pollution is not one of their functions.

s:
Arrange the following events in the chronological order from first to last.

I. All the buses of Delhi were converted to run on CNG.

II. Government of India passed the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act

III. Government of India introduced Joint forest Management.
src: TSPSC Polytechnic Lecturer 05-09-2023
x: Water Act 1974 (II) came first, Joint Forest Management 1990 (III) next, and Delhi's whole bus fleet ran on CNG by 2002 (I) last.

s:
Which of the following statement/s is/are correct about the National Green Tribunal (NGT):

A. The NGT shall consist of not less than five but subject to maximum of 10 full time judicial members.

B. To be appointed as the Chairperson of the Tribunal, a person must be a judge of the Supreme Court or the High Court.
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: The NGT Act provides for not less than 10 and up to 20 full-time judicial members (and as many expert members), not 5 to 10. The Chairperson must be or have been a Supreme Court judge or the Chief Justice of a High Court, so an ordinary High Court judge does not qualify. Both statements are wrong.

s:
Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about the Large Forest Fire Monitoring Programme launched in 2019?
Statement A: Forest Survey of India launched the beta version of the programme on 16-01-2019 using near real-time SNPP-VIIRS data.
Statement B: This programme is a part of the FAST 5.0 (FSI Fire Alerts System).
Statement C: FSI will track large fire events across the country and disseminate specific Large Fire alerts.
src: APPSC Group-IV Paper-I (Mains) General Studies & Mental Abil
x: The Forest Survey of India launched the Large Forest Fire Monitoring Programme (beta, 16 Jan 2019) using near-real-time SNPP-VIIRS data to track large fires and send large-fire alerts. It is part of FAST 3.0 (Forest Fire Alert System), not 'FAST 5.0', so only B is incorrect.

s: As per the analysis of water quality by Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board (APPCB), the quality of water in all major rivers in Andhra Pradesh falls under ____ category.
src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
x: APPCB monitoring has placed river water in Andhra Pradesh in Class 'C' (drinkable only after conventional treatment and disinfection), mainly because of high coliform counts.

s: The UN Sustainable Development Goals came into force in 2016. When are they due to expire?
src: APPSC Dental Asst. Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Officers,
x: The SDGs, in force from 2016, are due to be achieved by 2030.

s: The United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED), Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil was organised during:
src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrogeology) in AP Ground Water
x: The Rio Earth Summit (UNCED) was held on 3-14 June 1992.

s: Which of the following city was the venue of the World Sustainable Development Summit 2019?
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: TERI's World Sustainable Development Summit is held in New Delhi every year, including 2019.

s: Which of the following three R's are regarded as environment friendly?
src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
x: The environment-friendly 3 Rs are Reduce, Reuse and Recycle – the basis of the circular economy.

s: Which of the following is the best fire extinguisher in the case of electrical fire?
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
x: CO2 is the best extinguisher for electrical fires: it does not conduct electricity and leaves no residue. Water and soda-acid conduct electricity.

s:
Which of the following statement/s is/are correct about the Biodiversity?

A. The genetic diversity enables the population to adapt to its environment and to respond to natural selection.

B. Gamma diversity is related with the diversity of the habitant happened over the total geographical area.
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: Genetic diversity lets a population adapt and respond to natural selection (A), and gamma diversity is the diversity of habitats over a whole geographical area (B), so both are correct.

s: Which of the following agency published the Red data book?
src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
x: The Red Data Book is published by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN).

s: Select the correct match Wild Life Sanctuary areas in Andhra Pradesh
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: Rollapadu Wildlife (Bird) Sanctuary is in Kurnool (now Nandyal) district, AP, known for the Great Indian Bustard. (AP protected-area item, moved.)

s:
Consider the following statements about 'Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary':

a. It is the third largest stretch of mangrove forests in India.

b. It is home to the critically endangered white-backed vulture and the long billed vulture.
Which of the following statement/s is/are correct?
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x:
Official key / most books: only b (Coringa = 'second-largest mangrove'). Strictly: rankings differ – PMF Environment 02 p.57 ranks Bhitarkanika second, which would make Coringa third and statement a true too.
Statement b is right: Coringa hosts the critically endangered white-backed and long-billed vultures. Statement a is wrong in the key's reading – Coringa is usually called the second-largest m

s: Crocodile 2. Elephant Which of these is/are endangered species ?
src: I.A.S. (Pre) 2003
x:
Official key / most books: both. Strictly: Asian elephant = EN, but of India's crocodiles only the gharial is threatened (CR); mugger = VU and saltwater crocodile = LC (PMF Environment 03 p.99).
The key treats both as endangered: the Asian elephant is IUCN Endangered, and India's crocodilians (the gharial is Critically Endangered) are protected as threatened species.

s: The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 provides legal framework for the protection of wild animals only. 2. Project Elephant aim to conserve wild Asian elephants only.
src: UP R.O./A.R.O. (Pre) 2023
x: Both are wrong: the WPA 1972 protects wild animals, birds and plants, and Project Elephant also covers the welfare of captive elephants.

s: Which of the following is the most abundant Greenhouse- Gas found in the earth's atmosphere?
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: Water vapour is the most abundant greenhouse gas in the atmosphere.

s: It means that a country will bring down its emissions to zero by 2050. 2. It means that a country's emissions will be compensated by the absorption and removal of greenhouse gases from the atmosphere. Select the correct answer using the codes given below. Codes :
src: U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2021
x: Net zero means residual emissions are balanced by absorption and removal of greenhouse gases, so statement 2 is correct. It does not mean emissions fall to zero by 2050 for every country (India's year is 2070), so statement 1 is wrong.

s: When did the Bhopal Gas tragedy happen?
src: M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2013
x: The Bhopal gas tragedy occurred on the night of 2-3 December 1984.

s: Which of the following has highest pH?
src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
x: Human blood has a pH of about 7.4 (slightly basic), higher than the acidic or neutral items usually offered.

s: Name the project whose site in Chittoor district 'Mandaram Resource Centre' (MRC) includes a demonstration centre for alternative agriculture and sustainability practices and the volunteers work with local people and farmers, address local sustainability issues with solutions tailored to local conditions.
src: Junior Lecturers 2020
x: No source found that names the project running the Mandaram Resource Centre in Chittoor district; web searches for Mandaram returned nothing, so no option can be verified and the item stays unscored.

s: Which of the following bacteria helps in formation of curd?
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
x: Lactobacillus turns milk sugar into lactic acid and sets curd.

s: Which of the following scientist was part of the team that successfully cloned the first mammal named Dolly?
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
x: Dolly was cloned at the Roslin Institute by Ian Wilmut, Keith Campbell and colleagues.

s: Consider the following statements and choose the correct ones using the codes given below : A . The flavr-savr tomato was the first genetically engineered crop product to be commercialised. B . Ripe fruits of flavr-savr remain firm for longer duration and can be transported to market after vine-ripening. C . Ripe fruits of flavr-savr have colour but not the full array of vine ripened tomato flavours. Code :
src: R.A.S./R.T.S. (Pre) 2016
x: Flavr Savr was the first commercialised GE crop product; its antisense PG gene keeps ripe fruit firm so it can ripen on the vine and still be shipped (A, B). C is false - it was meant to keep the full vine-ripened flavour.

s: Which of the following are bio fertilizer
src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
x: Rhizobium, Azotobacter, blue-green algae, Azolla and mycorrhiza are all biofertilisers, so the printed answer 'All of above' holds (options not preserved).

s: With reference to Global alliance for Climate-Smart Agriculture (GACSA); which of the following statement is correct?
at: Membership of GACSA does not create any binding obligation
src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
x: GACSA, facilitated by FAO, is a voluntary alliance launched in 2014 (not Paris 2015); membership creates no binding obligations, so only this statement is correct (UPSC 2018).

s: Which of the following is a Bio drainage plant species?
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
x: Bio-drainage uses fast-growing, high-transpiring trees such as Eucalyptus to pump excess water from waterlogged land.

s: A normal gas stove lighter works on the principle of
src: APPSC Assistant Architectural Surveyor & Deputy Surveyor Gen
x: A gas-stove spark lighter strikes a piezoelectric crystal: pressure makes a high voltage that sparks; the Thomson and Joule effects are thermal.

s: Which of the following causes Tuberculosis?
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
x: Tuberculosis is caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

s: Which of the following is an air borne disease?
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
x: Airborne diseases such as tuberculosis, measles, influenza, chickenpox and the common cold spread through droplets or aerosols, so 'all of the above' (the options are not printed in this source).

s: Which of the following symptom is not associated with gastro intestinal disease?
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
x: GI diseases cause diarrhoea, vomiting, nausea and abdominal pain; kidney failure is not a GI symptom.

s:
Which of the following statements about Nafithromycin is/are correct?
1: Nafithromycin was officially launched on 20 November 2024 by Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh.
2: It was developed by Sun Pharma with support from the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR).
3: It is marketed as "Miqnaf" and is used to treat Community-Acquired Bacterial Pneumonia (CABP) caused by drug-resistant bacteria.
src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &

s: Which of the following childhood diseases CANNOT be prevented through a vaccine provided through the Universal Immunization Programme?
src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
x: Rickets is vitamin D deficiency and no vaccine prevents it; UIP vaccines cover infections such as TB, polio, measles, diphtheria.

s:
Consider the following statement:
(A) Air pollutants known as "PM 2.5" increases the chances of heart diseases.
(R) These micro particles can penetrate deep in lungs and enter in blood circulation.
at: Both correct and R explains A
src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspectors, Agriculture Office

s:

s: Which of the following is not a life style disease?
src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspectors, Agriculture Office
x: Malaria is a communicable disease caused by Plasmodium and spread by Anopheles mosquitoes, not a lifestyle disease like diabetes or hypertension.

s: Which of the following has anti-infective property?
src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
x: Colostrum, the first milk, is rich in antibodies (IgA) and has anti-infective properties.

s: Addition of selected nutrients not normally present in a particular food is called
src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
x: Adding selected nutrients not normally present in a food (iron, folic acid, vitamin B12, iodine) is food fortification.

s: The Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK) under the National Health Mission provides which of the following free entitlements for pregnant women?
at: Free C-section, provision of blood, drugs and diagnostics
src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
x: JSSK entitles pregnant women to free delivery including C-section, free drugs, diagnostics, blood, diet and transport at public facilities.

s: Which of the following is true in relation to Ayushman Bharat?
at: It will provide health care coverage up to Rs 5 lakh per family per year for hospitalization
src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspectors, Agriculture Office
x: PM-JAY under Ayushman Bharat gives cover of up to Rs 5 lakh per family per year for hospitalisation.
